CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. To make a very dark tone with charcoal you should (1 mark)
   A. press very lightly
   B. press harder
   C. use water
   D. use no charcoal

2. In a drawing of a drum with light from the left, which part is darkest? (1 mark)
   A. The side facing the light
   B. The white paper background always
   C. The side away from the light
   D. Nothing is dark

3. Which tool is good for smudging charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. A stone
   B. A knife
   C. A finger or a tissue
   D. A wet brush of paint

4. Which is a non-melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Marimba
   B. Xylophone
   C. Shaker
   D. Thumb piano

5. What is the main reason for improvising a netball? (1 mark)
   A. Because real balls are always bad
   B. To spend more money
   C. To avoid playing
   D. To use available materials when balls are not enough

6. How long may a player hold the ball before passing or shooting? (1 mark)
   A. Three seconds
   B. Ten seconds
   C. As long as they like
   D. One minute

7. How many players are in a full netball team on the court? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 11
   C. 7
   D. 9

8. In a double-handed catch, where should your eyes be? (1 mark)
   A. On the ball until it is in your hands
   B. On the crowd
   C. On the ground
   D. On the next player

9. Why should you take turns to talk about each other's work? (1 mark)
   A. To make others sad
   B. It is fair and respectful
   C. To waste time
   D. So no one speaks

10. Colour value means (1 mark)
   A. how light or dark a colour is
   B. the price of a colour
   C. the smell of paint
   D. how loud a colour is

11. Which colour is a secondary colour? (1 mark)
   A. Red
   B. Blue
   C. Green
   D. Yellow

12. Overlapping in a montage means (1 mark)
   A. pieces are cut into tiny bits
   B. pieces are painted black
   C. pieces are far apart
   D. one piece partly covers another

13. How many beats does a crotchet last? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Half
   C. Two
   D. One

14. How many claps are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa (rest)? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Four
   C. Six
   D. Five

15. When you see a crotchet rest, you should (1 mark)
   A. shout
   B. clap twice
   C. keep the beat but not clap
   D. stop the whole song

16. A pair of quavers together lasts (1 mark)
   A. one beat
   B. half a beat
   C. two beats
   D. four beats

17. What is the main purpose of hand signs when singing? (1 mark)
   A. To tell the time
   B. To show the pitch of the notes
   C. To keep flies away
   D. To count money

18. Pitch means (1 mark)
   A. the speed of a song
   B. how loud a sound is
   C. how high or low a sound is
   D. how long a sound lasts

19. The Kodaly hand sign for m is (1 mark)
   A. a closed fist
   B. a wave
   C. a flat palm held level
   D. a sloping palm

20. Which is the highest of the notes d, r and m? (1 mark)
   A. m
   B. r
   C. d
   D. They are all the same

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State two ways to keep the working area clean after painting. (2 marks)

22. Give the French rhythm names for a crotchet and a pair of quavers. (2 marks)

23. Describe the procedure of making charcoal sticks for drawing, from cutting to cooling. (5 marks)

24. Explain what overlapping is and why it is used in a montage. (3 marks)

25. What does it mean to improvise a rhythmic pattern? (3 marks)

26. Explain how a drum makes sound and how its parts work together. (5 marks)

27. Why do we scratch and wet clay before joining pieces? (3 marks)

28. Describe how you would improvise a rhythm to accompany a song. (4 marks)

29. Describe the Kodaly hand sign for each of d, r and m. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — press harder
   Pressing harder leaves more charcoal, so the tone is darker.

2. C — The side away from the light
   Shadows fall on the side away from the light, so it is darker.

3. C — A finger or a tissue
   A finger or tissue blends charcoal softly.

4. C — Shaker
   A shaker gives a rattling sound but not different notes for a tune.

5. D — To use available materials when balls are not enough
   Improvising lets us practise with materials we already have.

6. A — Three seconds
   A player must pass or shoot within three seconds.

7. C — 7
   A full netball team has seven players on court.

8. A — On the ball until it is in your hands
   Watching the ball helps you catch it.

9. B — It is fair and respectful
   Taking turns shows respect and love for others.

10. A — how light or dark a colour is
   Value is the lightness or darkness of a colour.

11. C — Green
   Green is made from yellow and blue.

12. D — one piece partly covers another
   Overlapping helps to fill gaps and make the montage full.

13. D — One
   A crotchet lasts for one beat.

14. D — Five
   Ta-te has two, ta-te has two, taa has one, and the rest has none, so five claps.

15. C — keep the beat but not clap
   A rest is a silent beat, and the beat continues.

16. A — one beat
   Two half beats make one whole beat.

17. B — To show the pitch of the notes
   Hand signs help singers see and remember how high a note is.

18. C — how high or low a sound is
   Pitch is the highness or lowness of a note.

19. C — a flat palm held level
   Me is shown with a flat, level hand.

20. A — m
   Me is the highest of the three.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wash the brushes and containers, wipe the desk, put the paper in the bin. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Crotchet: taa. Pair of quavers: ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Cut dry, straight twigs about the length of a hand. Trim off bark, knots and leaves. Pack the twigs tightly in a tin and close the lid with a small hole. An adult burns the tin in a fire until the smoke stops. Leave the tin closed to cool completely before opening.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cutting, trimming, packing, burning by an adult, and cooling.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Overlapping means placing one piece so it partly covers another. It removes gaps and makes the montage look full and joined up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reasons.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: To make up a pattern on the spot without writing it first, using an instrument such as a drum or shaker to keep to the beat of a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making up on the spot, 1 mark for no writing first, 1 mark for using an instrument.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: The beater or hand strikes the drumhead, which vibrates and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder. The ropes hold the skin tight, and a tighter skin gives a higher sound.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for striking, vibrating skin, shell, ropes, and effect of tightness on pitch.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes the surface rough and sticky so the pieces hold together and do not fall off when dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scratching, 1 mark for water, 1 mark for the reason.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing the song and find the beat by tapping. Play the beat on an instrument. Change to a pattern, such as two quick sounds and a long sound. Repeat it and change it at the end of a verse.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step, up to 4.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: d is a closed fist, r is a sloping palm, m is a flat palm held level.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
